title: HeLa: the first immortal human cell line
summary: Cells from Henrietta Lacks's cervical tumour became HeLa, the first human cells that kept dividing in the lab, and one of medicine's most important research tools.
why: Underpinned decades of research, from vaccines to cancer biology.

unsung.contribution: Her tumour cells became HeLa, the first immortalised human cell line.
unsung.recognition: Samples were taken without her permission or knowledge; her family was not told the cell line existed until 1975.
